clue.text: Ray has closure about a foreign bishop

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece holds the others within it
'about' means surrounding, so the outer piece goes round the inner ones

blocks.note: a seam is the join that closes two edges of cloth
un is French for 'a'
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A ray of light somehow bringing an end to a matter involving a bishop from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closure' suggests ending a matter, but here it is the stitched join that closes fabric. 'A foreign' asks for 'a' in another language, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a single shaft of sunlight, which is a ray in the plainest physical sense.

blocks.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation for school
an ism is any doctrine or belief system

explanation.surface: A split arising from a school of religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a doctrinal rift, but 'of' only joins the definition to two short abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or rupture within a group, especially a church, so it is a breach between factions.

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out of the word

blocks.note: a nuisance is an annoying pest
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: An insect leaving a shady spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' looks like a place in the surface, but it is the definition in its sense of a slight difference. NUISANCE minus IS leaves NUANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade of meaning is a subtle variation, and nuance is exactly that kind of fine distinction.

clue.text: Is last seen mixing food and drink?

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the order of these letters is scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: Someone is last spotted combining things to eat and drink, like a barman at closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: food and drink are instances of the basics of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Food and drink are the most basic necessities of life, things nobody can do without.

blocks.note: first meaning: chops are the jaws, as in 'lick your chops'
second meaning: sauce is cheeky backchat, impudent talk

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a dinner of lamb chops with gravy; both words switch to slang senses, the jaws and cheeky talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Chops is slang for the jaws or lips, and mouth also means insolent talk, which is what sauce means too.

indicators.note: what comes originally comes at the start, so each name contributes only its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of the name
first letter of the name
being quits with someone means being evens, owing nothing

explanation.surface: The nonsense poet Edward Lear walks out on a group of sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quits' looks like a verb about Lear leaving; it is the adjective meaning square or even with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket sides field eleven players each, so teams are often called elevens.

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
centric means centred on something

explanation.surface: A sales line for urban clothing aimed squarely at city dwellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' suggests clothing, but it is the engineering sense. The joke is that the word for off-centre is built as 'city-centred'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric is a disc mounted off its axis to turn rotation into back-and-forth motion, so it is a kind of mechanical gear.

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker famously drops the aitch at the start of words

blocks.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court

explanation.surface: A Londoner sampling flakes from a breakfast bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, which drops a leading H, so HEARS becomes 'EARS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear is the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant such as wheat or corn.

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters seed widely, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A transmitted programme gets duplicated in sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the TV-serial surface so well it reads as the subject, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something episodic is made up of separate episodes or instalments, which is to say it comes in parts.

clue.text: Transport to carry five around European border

indicators.note: a vehicle that carries something holds it inside, so other letters go within

blocks.note: a sledge is a vehicle on runners for snow
E is the abbreviation for European
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Instructions for a vehicle to take five people round a European frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The fit is loose: E and V do not enter as one unit but slot into SLEDGE at two points, E after the first letter and V after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A selvedge is the self-finished edge of woven fabric that stops it fraying, so it is a border of cloth.

blocks.note: first meaning: the call made when a coin is tossed
second meaning: the naval word for lavatories on a ship

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks someone to call out for the loo; 'Call' is instead the guess at a coin toss.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads is one of the two calls at a coin toss, and sailors call shipboard lavatories the heads.

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, and crazy letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy Cairn terrier yapping away is being aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cairn is a small Scottish terrier, which makes 'barking' look like a dog noise; it is the British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm and friendly, so uncordial is its opposite: unfriendly or hostile in manner.

blocks.note: to second staff is to transfer them temporarily to another post
a rating is an ordinary sailor, and a ship's hand is one too

explanation.surface: Something employed to move a score or grade elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used to' reads as one phrase, but 'Used' alone is the definition. Second here is stressed on the last syllable, as in a temporary posting.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are secondhand have had a previous owner, which is what used means of a car or book.

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by speech, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: to know someone is to recognise them

explanation.surface: Word is that someone has identified a man named Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name; it is the beak of a bird, a slang word for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's bill is its beak, and beak and bill are both informal words for a person's nose.

indicators.note: something fluid flows and changes shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A watery expanse somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the anagram signal 'Fluid' doubles as a description of a body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caspian is a vast inland body of water between Europe and Asia, a liquid expanse on the Asian side.

clue.text: Introductory procedure to exchange university degree

indicators.note: exchanging means swapping places, so the two parts trade positions

blocks.note: Reading is an English university town
a first is the top class of British honours degree

explanation.surface: A first step in the process of trading in one academic qualification for another.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the university before the degree, so the two parts must change places. A first is a top-class British honours degree; Reading is a town west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament a bill's first reading is the formal stage where it is introduced, so it is the opening procedure.

clue.text: Old ushers dressed up as bears

indicators.note: dressing up changes appearance, so these letters take on a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Elderly theatre attendants in costume as teddy bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals in a fancy-dress picture; it is the verb meaning carries a load.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden or responsibility is to take it on and carry it, which is what bears means.

indicators.note: goods stocked by a shop are held inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a homestead is a farmhouse with its land
ore is raw material dug from the ground

explanation.surface: Getting fabric ready that farmsteads keep in store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' suggests fabric, but here it means raw mineral matter dug from the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: To forearm someone is to arm or prepare them in advance, as in 'forewarned is forearmed'.

clue.text: Orthodox church priest interrupts work by editor

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in on something, so these letters break into the middle of another word

blocks.note: an act is a deed or piece of work
CE is the Church of England
P is an abbreviation for priest
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A cleric from an Eastern church breaks into an editor's project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orthodox church' reads as one name, the Eastern Orthodox Church, but 'Orthodox' alone is the definition and 'church' is the Church of England abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox views are those generally accepted as correct or standard, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Unfortunately lose piccolos and another instrument

indicators.note: a misfortune means things went wrong, so these letters end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An orchestra regrettably mislays its piccolos plus another instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests the orchestra of the surface, but the answer is a scientific instrument, not a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An oscilloscope is an electronic measuring device that displays waveforms on a screen, an instrument in the laboratory sense.

clue.text: Spike and Kelvin infiltrating municipal facility

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so one letter slips into another word

blocks.note: a sewer is a drain run by the town
K is the symbol for the kelvin temperature unit

explanation.surface: Two agents named Spike and Kelvin sneak into a council building.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike and Kelvin look like a pair of names; 'Spike' is the definition and 'and' merely joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a long pointed rod pushed through food for cooking, a kind of spike.

clue.text: Kept fourth shop in a row?

blocks.note: a store is a shop
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet
surface padding that sets up the picture of lettered shops along a street

explanation.surface: Kept the fourth shop along a terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the joke: shops labelled by letter along a row would make the fourth one 'store D'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stored and kept both mean put away and held for later use, as with goods in a warehouse.

indicators.note: a region is an area within something larger, so the letters lie inside the word

blocks.note: letters four to seven of the word

explanation.surface: Someone surveys a cartoon-like part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Region' looks like the noun the adjective describes; it signals a stretch inside the long word.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look it over carefully, so eyes means looks over in the present tense.

blocks.note: surface reading: an outfit so stylish that no critic could fault it
setter's reading: criticism is flak, so this is protective wear that stops flak

explanation.walkthrough: Flak is literally anti-aircraft fire and figuratively harsh criticism; the garment built to withstand the first is defined through the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A flak jacket is a reinforced protective vest worn against shrapnel and bullets, so it is clothing that resists flak.

clue.text: Cries when Nationalist brought up attacks

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing a letter up lifts it to an earlier place inside the word

blocks.note: to keen is to wail in grief
N is an abbreviation for Nationalist

explanation.surface: Wails follow when a nationalist is raised and then assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the N from the end of KEENS and move it up, in this down entry, to sit second.
explanation.definitionFit: To knee someone is to strike them with the knee, so knees is a verb meaning attacks physically.

indicators.note: removing something from a whole takes it out, leaving the rest behind

blocks.note: grottoes are caves
grot is British slang for rubbish or junk

explanation.surface: Litter cleared out of the far ends of caverns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremities' looks like it belongs with 'caves'' as the ends of caves, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Toes are at the very ends of the feet, so they are among the body's extremities.

clue.text: Hand back old children we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is taken by ear, so the sound matters and not the spelling

blocks.note: retro means harking back to an old style
seed means offspring, as in biblical language

explanation.surface: Return the former kids, so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed meaning descendants is an old biblical usage. RETROCEDE is a rare legal word: to cede territory back.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrocede is to cede back, returning territory to the state it came from, which is handing it back.

clue.text: One who joins partners in series

indicators.note: one thing inside another means these letters are placed within the outer word

blocks.note: SER is the abbreviation for series
East and West are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A person who links couples one after another, like a matchmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who joins partners' looks like a celebrant or matchmaker; the definition stops at 'joins'. Bridge is played by two pairs, North-South and East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer, said to rhyme with 'lower', is someone who sews, and sewing joins pieces of fabric together.

indicators.note: one thing inside another means these letters go within the outer word

blocks.note: SATs are national tests taken by schoolchildren in England
DIs are detective inspectors

explanation.surface: Someone harshly attacks officers in their performance reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savages' reads as a verb about mauling the police; it is the plural noun meaning brutal people.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadists take pleasure in cruelty, and savages are cruel, brutal people, so both are plural nouns for the vicious.

clue.text: Fought the German charges when retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters run the opposite way

blocks.note: der is German for 'the'
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: German troops fought by charging and then falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' suggests military attacks to go with 'Fought', but it means accusations.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or fight in practice, so sparred is a past-tense synonym for fought.
